nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## About this workflow

This template runs the **Image to Video** task (`MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo` node), which covers both:

- **t2va** (text-to-video), when no images are connected
- **fl2va** (first/last-frame image-to-video), when `first_frame` and/or `last_frame` are connected

**Key inputs**

- **first_frame / last_frame**: optional keyframes; the model generates the motion between them
- **prompt**: describe the shots, motion, and the accompanying audio (dialogue, SFX, music) in one block
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector. H3's native canvas is a 768px short edge, capped at 768x1344 pixels, rounded to a multiple of 32
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node, snapping up to the model's 17-frame-per-block (17k+5) grid at 24fps

widgets_values:
subject_definitions

<Subject 1> is Rick Sanchez, an elderly eccentric scientist with wild spiky pale-blue hair, a white lab coat, light-blue shirt, brown pants, and an impatient, slightly unhinged personality.

<Subject 2> is Morty Smith, a nervous teenage boy with short brown hair, a yellow T-shirt, blue jeans, and an anxious, hesitant personality.

summary

[Text-to-video] A 15-second animated sci-fi comedy scene featuring <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> inside Rick's cluttered garage laboratory. Rick unveils a suspicious new portal experiment while Morty immediately realizes something is wrong. The experiment escalates into a chaotic dimensional malfunction with fast comedic dialogue, expressive reactions, environmental destruction, and tight lip-sync.

retention_analysis

<Subject 1> ([Shot 1–4] / Rick): fully_preserved — Maintain identical facial design, clothing, proportions, pale-blue spiky hair, and energetic body language throughout every shot.

<Subject 2> ([Shot 1–4] / Morty): fully_preserved — Maintain identical facial design, yellow shirt, proportions, and nervous mannerisms throughout every shot.

detailed_description

[Shot 1 — 0–4s] Wide establishing shot inside a cluttered garage laboratory packed with strange machinery, cables, glowing screens, chemistry equipment, and half-finished inventions. <Subject 1> stands proudly beside a homemade portal machine covered in blinking lights. <Subject 2> watches from several feet away, visibly suspicious.

<Subject 1> excitedly slaps the side of the machine and says: <d>[English] Morty! I finally fixed interdimensional travel. No portal gun required!</d>

The machine begins emitting an ominous electrical hum.

[Shot 2 — 4–7s] Quick cut to a medium close-up of <Subject 2>. He looks from Rick to the violently shaking machine. A tiny electrical explosion pops behind him.

<Subject 2> stammers: <d>[English] Rick, why is it smoking?! Machines aren't supposed to smoke before you turn them on!</d>

The camera performs a quick comedic push-in as his eyes widen.

[Shot 3 — 7–11s] Smash cut to <Subject 1>. Rick looks annoyed rather than concerned. He grabs a large metal wrench and hits the machine once.

<Subject 1> says: <d>[English] That's not smoke, Morty. That's quantum exhaust. Completely differ—</d>

The machine suddenly activates with a deafening ZAP.

A huge unstable glowing green portal violently opens behind Rick. Wind blasts through the garage. Papers, tools, cans, and loose objects fly toward it.

[Shot 4 — 11–15s] Fast handheld two-shot. <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> desperately grab onto a workbench as the portal sucks objects out of the garage.

<Subject 2> screams: <d>[English] RICK! TURN IT OFF!</d>

Rick struggles to hold on while reaching toward the controls and shouts:

<Subject 1>: <d>[English] I'M TRYING, MORTY! THE OFF BUTTON WENT THROUGH THE PORTAL!</d>

A toaster flies between them and disappears into the portal.

Morty slowly turns toward Rick with an exhausted, furious expression.

Hard cut to black.

overall_soundscape

High-energy animated sci-fi sound design. Constant low laboratory electronics and fluorescent hum underneath the scene. Electrical crackling increases as the portal machine destabilizes. The portal activation produces a powerful dimensional blast followed by roaring wind, rattling metal, flying laboratory objects, glass clinks, and machinery alarms. Dialogue remains crisp and dominant with accurate character-specific lip-sync. No music and no laugh track.

visual_style

High-quality adult animated sci-fi sitcom aesthetic, bold outlines, flat cel-shaded colors, exaggerated facial expressions, detailed cluttered garage laboratory, energetic comedic timing, smooth character animation, dramatic green portal lighting reflecting across the characters and environment.

camera_direction

Begin with a stable wide establishing shot, cut to reaction close-ups during dialogue, use a rapid comedic push-in on Morty's worried reaction, smash cut to Rick immediately before the machine activates, then transition into subtle chaotic handheld camera movement during the portal malfunction. Maintain clear character framing and readable facial expressions throughout.

nodes.title: HOW TO REUSE THIS WORKFLOW
widgets_values: Change the first frame, last frame, FACE IDENTITY image, and BOTH prompt fields. The identity image should be a clear front-facing human face. This pass refines one identity. Duplicate the whole refine pass for another person.

nodes.title: DETECTOR LIMIT
widgets_values: The installed YOLO + InsightFace models work on photographic human faces. They failed on the local Rick and Morty cartoon images. Check the tracker preview/report before paying for the second H3 pass.

nodes.title: Frame Count and Shot Duration
widgets_values:
## Frame Count and Shot Duration

MiniMax H3 generates native 24 FPS batches on the 17k+5 grid. Face refinement uses the exact decoded batch count. RIFE 2x produces ((N-1)*2)+1 frames and the final node encodes at 48 FPS, preserving first-to-last-frame duration.

widgets_values:
Vaporwave title sequence look: pink and blue gradient palette, VHS tracking artifacts, Greek statue motifs, chrome palm trees, RGB chromatic aberration, lo-fi retro atmosphere, mood languid and nostalgic.

Timeline:
[0s-1s] VHS static opens the frame, the title "COMFYUI" appears with RGB split and a slight horizontal jitter.
[1s-2.5s] Hard cut, a Greek plaster bust close-up, pink-purple gradient sky, a pixelated sun.
[2.5s-4s] Clean "STARRING" credits appear, "LATENT" and "CONTROLNET" each shown exactly once.
[4s-5s] Final card "DIRECTED BY COMFYUI" holds, one VHS tracking glitch settling into stability.

Hard cuts only, transitions landing with tape jumps, no push-ins, no dissolves.

Audio: lo-fi vaporwave score, slow drum machine with soft bass, VHS tape-noise sample joins at 2.5s, melody fading for the last 1s.

All text must be clearly legible, do not misspell English, no Chinese characters, do not repeat names or job titles, no soft dissolves, no subtitle bars.
